image_description: A white minibus parked on a paved street next to a curb and a white bollard. The vehicle features a boxy design typical of shuttle buses, with a large front windshield, a destination display above the windshield, side windows along the passenger area, and visible wheels. A brick building and greenery are in the background.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Boxy body shape noticeably shorter than a full-size bus, yet tall enough for passengers to stand or sit upright comfortably.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The vehicle clearly exhibits a compact, boxy silhouette distinct from full-size city buses, with sufficient roof height for standing room.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Large windshield and row of side windows along passenger area.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: A large, single-pane windshield is prominent, and multiple rectangular side windows are visible along the right side of the vehicle.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Height is substantial, with entrance door at front or mid-body.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The vehicle has significant vertical height relative to its width. A door frame/handle structure is visible near the front wheel arch, consistent with a front/mid-entry configuration.
Vertical seams and handles indicative of a sliding or folding door mechanism are visible on the side near the front axle.
The short hood and grille arrangement ahead of the windshield indicate a conventional front-engine layout.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Rear flat or slightly angled panel with taillights and license plate mount.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The rear of the vehicle is occluded by the viewing angle; only the front and right side are visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: White, yellow, or company livery paint with route markings.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bus is painted white with a blue stripe/livery and features an illuminated destination sign, matching typical transit aesthetics.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Standard van-sized wheels with steel or alloy rims.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible front and rear wheels are proportional to a light commercial vehicle chassis, appearing as standard steel rims with hubcaps.
The window count and overall dimensions align with the capacity range of a minibus (approx. 6-8 side windows suggesting seating rows).

artifact_observations.reasoning: The characters on the license plate are distorted and nonsensical ('B3...'), lacking the crisp geometry of real alphanumeric characters. This is a common AI artifact.
The text on the orange LED display is blurry and illegible, resembling generic pixel patterns rather than specific letters.

artifact_observations.location: Right side mirror and door handle area
artifact_observations.reasoning: Slight softness and lack of sharp mechanical definition in the mirror housing and door handles compared to the rest of the bodywork.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific vehicle class and distinguish it from similar vans or full-size buses.
To rigorously evaluate the severity of the text artifacts observed on the plate and header.
To verify that the wheels are properly grounded and not floating or melting into the pavement.
To check for edge bleeding or fusion between the appendages and the main body.

focus_areas: Text legibility on license plate and destination board
Structural integrity of wheels and suspension geometry
Sharpness of boundary lines on side mirrors and doors
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the license plate text; while the vehicle structure is sound, AI models often fail at rendering coherent text. Determine if the text gibberish significantly impacts the overall utility of the image or if it is a minor aesthetic flaw. Verify if the 'minibus' classification holds up against scrutiny of the wheelbase and window count.
